messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected in prod-usw2. p95 ~ 480ms, p99 spiking > 2.1s for streaming endpoints. alerts: streaming_stalls, tail_latency_surge. paging @eng-oncall :rotating_light:

alex: seeing a sharp spike in KV eviction rate on shard group g-41, eviction/sec ~ 420 (baseline ~12). streaming clients hit tail stalls when prefill misses + decode backlog.

maria: grabbing dashboards now — looks like prefill queue depth went from 0->800 over 10m, decode workers backlogged. also flag: prefill/decodes are uneven across cohorts (hf-models and small-seq).

sam: can we confirm if this is caused by recent prefill rollout? I deployed the prefill prioritizer yesterday morning.

alex: correlates with that timeframe. timeline: 10:07 prefill prioritizer enabled, 10:20 latency alerts begin. also noticed KV fragment counts per shard doubled.

irene: logs from a decode worker: ```ERROR: decode_queue_timeout: msg_id=0x7f3fd, waiting=4100ms
stack: worker=decode-eu-2, model=redwood-13b-quant```
messages_continued:
maria: adding more snippets — eviction log excerpt: ```[10:22:13] shard=g-41 eviction_count=421 reason=frag_threshold breached_by=2.1% prefill_rate=3k/s decode_rate=150/s```

sam: that prefill_rate looks insane. Could be a hot-key pattern causing heavy prefill churn and fragmentation. Anyone see client-side spikes?

megan: customer telemetry shows a burst from a single embedder job from acct:acme-ops — sustained small requests with high context length. might be hammering KV with unique prefixes.

alex: mitigation plan proposal: 1) throttle prefill from acme-ops via route-level rate limit 2) enable short-term KV-eviction-pause (experimental) to let decode catch up 3) scale decode workers by +30% 4) roll back prioritizer if needed. thoughts?

maria: thumbs on 1 and 3. eviction-pause is risky but buys time. sam, can you enable pause on g-41?

sam: doing it now. command: ```/run admin-kv --shard g-41 --eviction-pause 300s --reason "decode-backlog"```

oncall-bot: ACTION LOGGED: sam executed admin-kv (eviction-pause) at 3167894387.

irene: I pushed a temporary route limit for acct:acme-ops -> 50 rps. applied to prod-usw2 at 3167894399.

megan: customer notified via support. message queued: "We observed elevated latency, throttling a noisy job to restore cluster health. ETA 15-30m."

alex: decode worker scaleup started (autoscale triggered +6 workers) at 3167894412.

maria: dashboards starting to look better: prefill queue depth dropping, decode backlog trending down. p99 down to ~1.1s. still above SLO but improving.

sam: eviction rate on g-41 falling to ~18/s. Good signal that pause helped.

alex: quick postmortem notes while fresh: potential root causes: - prefill prioritizer interaction with long-context noisy client -> hot-prefix churn - KV fragmentation due to many unique keys + aggressive prefill causing high eviction churn - decode capacity under-provisioned for sudden prefill bursts

maria: follow-ups: 1) revert prioritizer change and run canary with batching limits 2) implement route-level circuit-breaker for extreme prefill rates 3) investigate compacting background job to defrag KV shards 4) add better telemetry: prefill->eviction correlation metric

megan: schedule customer follow-up call in 2 hours, include SRE + product + SE.

irene: oncall handoff note for night: if p99 rises above 1.5s again, escalate to eng-sre and trigger full rollback. leaving a runbook link: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/kv-eviction-mitigation

alex: thanks all. keeping thread open for final wrap at 3167894480. :white_check_mark:
